questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: conjugate a regular -er verb in the present tense

stimulus.body: Dans un exercice de français, le professeur demande de choisir la forme qui convient d'après la règle de la leçon.

questions.stem: In a problem set, a reviewer records the evidence: Quelle réponse applique correctement la règle de la leçon ?

options.misconception: uses the third person plural ending
uses the second person plural ending instead of the first
uses the third person singular ending

questions.explanation: Regular -er verbs take -ons in the first person plural, giving nous parlons. The key is C, "Nous parlons". Option A ("Nous parlent") is wrong: uses the third person plural ending. Option B ("Nous parlez") is wrong: uses the second person plural ending instead of the first. Option D ("Nous parle") is wrong: uses the third person singular ending.

questions.stem: In a reading group, a reviewer records the evidence: Quelle réponse applique correctement la règle de la leçon ?

options.misconception: uses the infinitive instead of a conjugated form
uses the third person singular ending
uses the second person singular ending

questions.explanation: Regular -ir verbs take -issent in the third person plural, giving ils finissent. The distractors are an infinitive, a tu form, and an il form of the same verb.
questions.hint: Third person plural of -ir verbs ends in -issent.

questions.explanation: Regular -re verbs take -s in the first person singular, giving je vends. The key is A, "Je vends". Option B ("Je vend") is wrong: omits the first person singular -s ending. options.misconception: uses a lexical verb instead of an auxiliary

questions.explanation: Motion and state-change verbs such as aller take être as their auxiliary in the passe compose. The distractors are the default auxiliary for most verbs, an unrelated lexical verb, and a near-synonym that is not the auxiliary.
